the effects of Rh doping and hydrostatic pressure on the magnetic and electronic properties of RuSr 2 Gd Cu 2 O 6+ x.

the study of the effect of Rh doping on the superconducting and magnetic properties of the ferromagnetic material RuSr 2 Gd Cu 2 O 7− x and its relation to the effect of hydrostatic pressure on the same system.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effect of pressure on superconductivity and on ferromagnetism is similar to that observed in the parent compound RuSr 2 Gd 2 O 6, and that pressure promotes the inter-granular coupling in the material, which is beneficial to its superconducting performance.
the effect of pressure on RuSr 2 Gd Cu 2 O 9− x is similar to the effect of doping, but with opposite sign, and therefore the two effects are not equivalent.

, while the superconductivity and magnetic properties of Ru 1−x Rh x Sr 1−x Gd x Cu 2 O 6−δ are strongly affected by the substitution of Ru by Rh and by the Gd doping, the pressure study indicates that the competition between the superconductivity, magnetism, and granularity is not affected by the Rh doping and the Gd doping.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pressure enhances both intra- and intergranular connectivity, and the superconductivity in these materials.
the effect of pressure on superconductivity in Ru 1−x Rh x Sr 1.9 GdCu 1.9 O 8 is to improve connectivity between grains and to increase T c, T m and T p.
the ferromagnetic superconductor RuSr 2 Gd Cu 2 O 7.5 is a very interesting material for the study of competition between ferromagnetism and superconductivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ferromagnetic superconductor RuSr 2 Gd 1− y Dy y Cu 2 O 10−δ is a promising candidate for a pressure sensor.
the ferromagnetic and superconducting properties of Ru 1−x Rh x Sr 1.5 GdCu 1.5 O 8 are sensitive to hydrostatic pressure, and that this sensitivity is dependent on the Rh content.
the superconducting and magnetic properties of these materials could be tuned by pressure, as a result of the modification of the electronic structure of the CuO 2 planes.
